confidence_note: From memory and secondary summaries; book text not accessed. Expected net worth formula (age x pre-tax income from all sources except inheritance / 10), PAW at least twice expected, UAW less than half confirmed by multiple secondary sources. Co-author William Danko omitted per brief. Millionaires living modestly and high earners with low net worth are stated as tendencies ('many'). Old TR claims (Stanley first searched luxury neighborhoods, PAWs hide their wealth, disregard status spending) not verified and dropped. DB title is Turkish 'Komsu Milyoner'.
facts: Many millionaires lived in ordinary houses and drove ordinary cars; many high earners had little saved.
Expected net worth = age x annual pre-tax income (excluding inheritance) / 10.
PAW: net worth at least twice expected.
UAW: net worth less than half expected.
PAWs live below their means and invest steadily.
The formula is a rule of thumb.
scene_details: age times income divided by ten
a new car and thin balance sheet
tension: High income and large wealth often differ.

lessons.idea: Compare savings to income, not neighbors.

reflect_final: If you compared what you have saved with what you have earned over the years, what would that comparison tell you?
pocket_idea: Compare what you've kept with what you've earned.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Two people with the same paycheck can be far apart in wealth.
